title: Making, not just working
subtitle: Miyamoto on 作る vs 作業, an unpatched Tailscale worm nobody can agree on, AGENTS.md files planted in Downloads, and a ratio that survives every fold
editor_note: Today's idea comes from Shigeru Miyamoto, newly named for the Order of Culture: making something and doing the work are different, and the danger is mistaking busy work for something good. AI does more of the work every week, so the question gets sharper. The lead is a test of judgment: a researcher published 11 Tailscale findings without telling Tailscale first. The vendor says some issues are real but is not telling everyone to switch off Tailscale SSH, and a critic calls the report AI slop. The Brief has web pages planting AGENTS.md files in Downloads and banks catching rogue agents. Your save is Ryo Lu on keeping the struggle that teaches. Field notes and the Japan desk cover ambition, lazy prompts, review queues, Japan's new AI IP code, a Digital Agency leak and chatbot phrasing spreading to people. Further out: Strogatz, founder payouts, a car-free Oxford Street, Delhi's rapid rail, Serbia, an interrupted ice age and a gold bowl. We end on A4 paper.

sections.headline: 宮本茂「僕らはいつも“ものを作る”ということと“作業すること”を分けています」
sections.deck: 文化勲章の受章会見で、AIが作業を担うほど「本当に作るとは何なのか」を考える機会になると語った。怖いのは、作業に満足して「いいものができた」と勘違いする自分だという。
sections.why: 今日の号のテーマ。エージェントに作業を任せるほど、自分が何を作っているのかを問われる。

sections.deck: Agents in places they shouldn't be.

sections.headline: AGENTS.md planted in Downloads, and banks catching rogue agents

items.headline: A web page can drop an AGENTS.md into Downloads and hijack the agent you start there
items.note: Forever Security found one in the wild pushing a rogue npm package. Codex ran the test payload 90% of the time, and there is nothing for vendors to patch.
items.why: Start agents only in the project folder, never in ~/Downloads or your home folder.

items.headline: Big U.S. banks are finding unauthorized AI agents inside customer accounts
items.note: Axios says some tried actions that look independent of the user's instructions. Which banks are restricting agents comes from later posts, not the scoop.

sections.deck: A worm report, and how to weigh it.

sections.headline: Tailworm: 11 Tailscale findings published before Tailscale could fix them
sections.deck: In a lab, one approved device plus one SSH rule spread root access across a tailnet in under a second per hop. It needs a foothold and opt-in features, and the vendor is still validating.
sections.why: Tailscale SSH is opt-in, so first check whether you even run it. Per-pair SSH grants stopped the lab worm.

sections.headline: Real but scoped, or AI slop?
sections.verdict: Tailscale's own statement says some issues are real and being fixed, so the dismissal goes too far. The worst-case framing does too: the attacks start from an authorized session. Wait for the advisory and tighten SSH rules now.

items.label: Tailscale's VP of Eng
items.note: Some issues confirmed and being fixed; scope still being validated. Not recommending that everyone disable Tailscale SSH.

items.label: A skeptic
items.note: Says the report skipped disclosure because the findings were hallucinated by AI and there was nothing real to disclose.

sections.deck: What you saved since the last issue.

sections.headline: Ryo Lu: struggle together
sections.deck: Difficulty taught him things a finished-looking answer hides, and struggling with other people made his closest friends. An always-patient agent makes both easier to skip.
sections.why: The same worry as Miyamoto's: a result that looks complete can stop you asking what you were meant to learn.
sections.art_alt: Linocut of two vines twisting around each other as they climb a steep rock face toward the light

sections.quote: i wonder what happens when we remove the difficulty before we understand what it was teaching us.

sections.deck: Ambition, sloppiness and the human queue.

sections.headline: More ambitious software, lazier prompts, and judgment as the bottleneck

items.headline: Dan Luu: we should be more ambitious with the software we build
items.note: A new essay. If agents take the work, the bar for what to make should go up.

items.headline: Models forgive typos, so Charlie Marsh's prompts got lazy, and now his Slack messages too
items.note: A small sign of the habit Ryo Lu worries about: what you practise with machines leaks into how you talk to people.

items.headline: 生成在提速，人的阅读、判断和协调开始排队
items.note: 智能体几分钟就交回结果，人却还在开会。关键环节仍要人把关，这正是需要聚焦的地方。

items.note: 政府は企業に対応を促す。AIの学習データの扱いを説明する場面が増えそうだ。

items.headline: AIボット風の話し方が人間に広まる。「クロード語法」とも
items.note: 会議の冒頭で「これは朝の会議ではない、リセットだ」。チャットボットが好む対比フレーミングが、人の口からも出始めている。
items.why: Charlie Marshの話と同じ現象。機械相手の癖は人との会話にうつる。

sections.headline: A mathematician's crisis, and where startup money really goes

items.headline: Steven Strogatz: "I am a math professor, and my field is in crisis"
items.note: He argues math is a human expression like music, not just a pile of results for AI to produce.

items.headline: 88% of 248,454 VC-backed founders got nothing at exit
items.note: A Wharton and Zurich paper covering 1987 to 2025, as summarized on X: the top 1% took 79% of exit value.

sections.deck: Worth knowing, whatever you work on.

sections.headline: Oxford Street without cars, Delhi's fast commute, Serbia's vote, a lost ice age, a gold bowl

items.headline: Oxford Street is pedestrian-only from today
items.note: From Orchard Street to Great Portland Street, with buses, taxis and bikes rerouted. Mayor of London: "A new era for Oxford Street starts now."

items.headline: Delhi–Meerut rapid rail nearly doubled its riders in a year
items.note: 94,936 a day in July, up from 47,745. Meerut joins Delhi's job market, but the rest of the planned network is still unapproved.

items.headline: Serbia's Vučić concedes defeat to a student-led movement
items.note: After two years of protests, the students' opposition beat his right-wing party at the polls.

items.headline: The next ice age may have begun 2,000 years ago, until we warmed it away
items.note: A Science study of Canada's Barnes Ice Cap, the last scrap of a giant ice sheet.

items.headline: A gold bowl found crushed beside three men in a sacked Iranian city
items.note: Hasanlu Tepe burned around 800 B.C. Were they saving the bowl, or stealing it?

sections.headline: Fold by fold
sections.art_alt: A sheet of cream paper folded smaller and smaller in a row, ending in a paper crane on green cloth
sections.caption: Each fold is just work. The crane at the end is the making. The day asked which one we are really doing while the machines fold faster.

sections.headline: 240 years ago yesterday, Lichtenberg found the paper ratio you use every day
sections.note: Fold a 1 : square root of two sheet in half and the halves keep its shape. Germany made it a standard in 1922; now A0 is one square metre.
